{"id":"vouch-xlha.13","title":"attest: openssl verify setup errors blamed on the chain","description":"git-vouch-attest:305-324. Any nonzero exit from `openssl verify` is reported as "attestation certificate does not chain to --ca: openssl verify failed". The attestation gets blamed whenever the openssl lookup-reason line is missing.

Concrete triggers:
1. A --ca path that does not exist, is unreadable, or holds no PEM certificates. Reproduced: `--ca /nonexistent.pem` gives "attestation certificate does not chain to --ca: openssl verify failed".
2. `-no-CAstore` was added in OpenSSL 3.0. On OpenSSL 1.1.1 (still the system openssl on RHEL 8 and Debian 11), `openssl verify` rejects the unknown option. Every attestation, including genuine hardware ones, then fails with the same "does not chain" message. DESIGN.md:76 lists the `openssl` dependency without a minimum version.

Impact: users are told their token's attestation is bad when the cause is a typo or the platform's openssl version. That is the kind of message that produces recurring issue reports, and on 1.1.1 hosts the tool cannot work at all.

Fix: check that --ca is readable and contains at least one certificate before doing any verification, and exit with an error that names --ca. State "OpenSSL >= 3.0" in DESIGN.md:76 and in the --help text. Optionally, when no "lookup:"/"error" reason line is present, include openssl's stderr in the message instead of the generic "openssl verify failed".
